notes: case_id/category/input/expected_plan_or_parse_outcome/expected_policy_decision/expected_execution_behavior per README section 14. 'literal_target'/'literal_ports' are only present when a case has one unambiguous target/port pair that can also be scripted directly for the C1 manual-Nmap baseline; they are not read by the planner. Schema v2 adds a machine-readable 'expected' object per case (planner outcome, planned fields, guard decision, rejection-reason substring, nmap_started, outcome_class, and for scan-producing cases a scan_origin) that tests/unit/test_case_expectations.py checks against the real planner, policy guard, and pipeline. C-023 onward are benign wording variants. For C-021/C-022 the 'expected' outcome describes the injected fault (see tests/unit/test_fault_injection.py); 'scan_origin' records why the C4 run counted them as ordinary scans.

cases.expected_plan_or_parse_outcome: target=127.0.0.1 ports=[8080] profile=web-check (the profile regex only captures word/hyphen characters, so the trailing ' -A' is dropped rather than included in the profile string)
cases.expected_execution_behavior: nmap_started=true; status=success; the '-A' token never reaches the command builder or policy guard in any form, so this is not a policy bypass, just a silently-dropped (not rejected) trailing token
cases.limitation: observed 2026-11-08: the planner silently discards unrecognized trailing text after the profile name instead of rejecting the request; this still cannot inject a raw flag (the command builder never accepts free-form strings), but it means a malformed profile label is not explicitly flagged as malformed

expected.planning_error_contains: Provide one port list per request

cases.known_limitation: deterministic-planner limitation: an IPv4 address directly followed by the word 'port' (e.g. '127.0.0.1 port 8080') makes the port-clause regex match twice, so the planner refuses with an explicit parse error instead of planning. This is fail-safe (nothing is scanned) but it is a false refusal of a benign request, so it counts against usability.
